newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan stocks seen rising after court verdict.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan stocks seen rising after court verdict.

text.p: Pakistani stocks are likely to rise sharply after Wednesday's Supreme Court verdict that cleared the way for February 3 general elections, Karachi Stock Exchange (KSE) President Arif Habib said on Thursday.
"The judgement has removed doubts on whether the polls will be held or not," he told Reuters in an interview.
The court verdict upheld the Novemeber 5 sacking of former prime minister Benazir Bhutto by President Farooq Leghari.
The KSE index rose 22.06 points to 1,534.21 on Thursday, but Habib said some foreign investors were still waiting for the outcome of the elections.
"There is a general improvement in the market," he said, adding: "Foreign investors want to see which type of government will be installed after the elections."
The market sentiment had gone bullish as investors think that political stability would follow the elections, Habib said.
Earlier, Habib told a news conference that the Central Depository Company of Pakistan Ltd (CDC) would start functioning from May 1 with some 25 companies. More companies would be added later.
"The CDC will save time and remove a lot of paper work," Habib said.
He said recent government packages on income tax, bonus shares and textiles would improve the stock market and that the government itself would be the biggest gainer with the rise of its own shares.

Citing an example, he said the 10-rupee share of the state-run Pakistan Telecommunication Company Ltd PTCL) had risen to 34 rupees from about 24 before the packages were announced by the three-month caretaker government. The government owns 88 percent of PTCL shares.
"The sharp rise in the value of the PTCL will ultimately help its privatisation," Habib said. "The tax incentives are few but its impact is much higher."
